lines.text: Here's how Claude made claude dot A I three times faster in two weeks, in under sixty seconds.
Say the message box is slow, because you can't type until the page loads.
First, someone reports the slow spot. Second, Claude builds a benchmark that reproduces it. Third, Claude opens small pull requests behind a flag, an on-off switch, and watches real-world timings.
The benchmark counts CPU instructions, not milliseconds, because clock timing is too noisy.
If it got faster, a daily job lowers the allowed count, and any pull request that raises it fails. If not, the flag goes off and Claude tries again.
One fix bakes an HTML copy of the message box into the page, so you can type while the rest loads.
Overall, the wait before you can type fell from three point one seconds to about half a second, and a person approved every change.
